title: Timing of Access Closure in Transfemoral Impella Care
summary:
The Impella is a small heart pump that is temporarily inserted into the heart via the femoral artery in the groin. By pumping blood from the left ventricle into the main artery, it relieves the left ventricle and improves blood flow to the organs. This creates time to specifically treat the cause of the heart disease, for example a heart attack caused by blocked coronary arteries.
Studies have shown that patients with cardiogenic shock, meaning shock due to reduced heart function, may have better survival when treated with an Impella. However, bleeding occurred more frequently, particularly at the vascular access site in the groin. Bleeding may be promoted, among other factors, by the large diameter of the Impella introducer sheath and by the necessary blood-thinning medication, called anticoagulation, which is used to prevent blood clots from forming and blocking the pump.
After removal of the Impella pump, also called explantation, an opening would remain in the femoral artery. We therefore use suture-based closure systems to close this opening. Suture-based closure systems are used to close the opening in the femoral artery in a minimally invasive way using a suture. The suture can already be placed at the time of Impella implantation and must be placed no later than at the time of Impella explantation. However, many bleeding events do not occur only after removal of the Impella pump, but already while the Impella pump is still in place in the groin. We therefore aim to investigate whether the timing of suture placement — at the time of Impella implantation versus only at the time of Impella explantation — may affect the occurrence of bleeding or other vascular complications.
Important: The study does not change the fact that a suture-based system is used for vascular closure; only the timing of suture placement is being investigated.

interventions.name: 50 patients with deployment of the suture-based vascular closure system already at the time of Impella implantation
50 patients with deployment of the suture-based vascular closure system only at the time of Impella explantation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Transfemoral Impella implantation
Exclusion criteria:
- Mechanical aortic valve replacement
- Severe peripheral arterial disease precluding transfemoral Impella implantation
